extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties and counsel involved in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) proceedings, and USPTO/PTAB adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing mandated discovery, misrepresentations, misleading arguments, and potential sanctions in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) Director Review proceedings, including guidance on expert availability, joinder/time-bar exceptions, and briefing for show-cause remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to comply with Mandated Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties ordered to answer interrogatories and produce categories of documents (e.g., formation and business documents of petitioner, documents/communications relating to filing/settlement/termination of the proceeding, and communications about experts) must comply with Mandated Discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandated Discovery was ordered “to allow all parties to answer the questions” set forth in the Scheduling Order; failure to comply may be sanctionable. The Scheduling Order warned that sanctions may be considered for any misrepresentation, exaggeration, or over-statement as to the facts or law made in the parties’ briefing and that attempts to withhold evidence based on a narrow interpretation of discovery requests may, alone or combined with other conduct, be sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege log and withholding procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Legitimate, lawful grounds for withholding documents may be lodged, but a party that withholds documents must maintain a privilege log of documents withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No responsive document may be withheld without being included in a privilege log. Parties were reminded they may lodge privilege objections but must still produce a log; withholding without a log may be sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation of fact and misleading argument (sanctionable conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: A misleading argument or misrepresentation of fact is sanctionable under 37 C.F.R. § 42.12(a)(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include representing in a petition that an expert was 'exclusively' engaged (such that a competing petitioner could not present the expert for cross-examination) when the engagement was waivable, or making inconsistent characterizations across filings. The Office will consider whether statements were literally false, misleading in context, or inconsistent in a way that influenced Board action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal relevance of misrepresentations to Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a representation influenced the Board's disposition (e.g., denial of a competing petition) is a relevant factor in assessing sanctionable misrepresentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director found PQA's statements regarding exclusivity materially influenced the Board's denial of OpenSky's petition; such causal links weigh in favor of sanctions. Parties should ensure accuracy of statements that the Board may rely upon in dispositive rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for expert availability for cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be deficient if it brings forth the testimony of an expert that likely cannot be produced for cross-examination, and such unavailability can warrant denial of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board examines facts showing whether an expert would likely be available for cross-examination (e.g., exclusivity agreements, communications). Assertions that an expert 'cannot' be presented should be accurate and any qualifications (e.g., waivable exclusivity) should be disclosed; failing to do so can be misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and completeness of disclosures supporting petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Material facts (e.g., existence and scope of exclusivity provisions in expert engagement agreements) supporting petition arguments should be timely and fully disclosed in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations made in the petition and in declarations are relied upon; disclosure of caveats after institution or only in pre-institution reply may be insufficient and can be misleading. Parties should include material limitations (such as waivable clauses) in initial filings where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director/Board discretion to deny institution or terminate for abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director and Board retain discretion to deny institution of AIA proceedings or terminate instituted trials when abuse of process is demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director's Scheduling Order asked parties to address what action should be taken when faced with evidence of abuse of process and how to assess conduct constituting abuse. Remedies should suit the wrongdoing and deter similar misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authorization for sanctioning abusive conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA (35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(6)) grants the Office broad authority to prescribe regulations sanctioning 'abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or any other improper use of the proceeding, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or an unnecessary increase in the cost of the proceeding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority underpins the Office's ability to sanction a wide range of misconduct; parties should be mindful of the statute when litigating strategy and discovery positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory sanctions available under 37 C.F.R. § 42.12
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide a broad range of potential sanctions for failure to comply with an applicable order or for misrepresentations/misleading arguments, including awarding 'compensatory expenses' and '[j]udgment in the trial.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enumerated sanctions in § 42.12(a)(1)–(3), (6), (b) are not exclusive; courts (e.g., Federal Circuit) have recognized the Board may issue sanctions not explicitly listed. Remedies include admonishment, reprimand, compensatory expenses (including attorney fees), dismissal of party, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show-cause briefing procedure for imposing compensatory expenses or admonishment
rubrics_metrics.description: When sanctionable conduct is found or suspected, the Director may order the party to 'show cause' why compensatory expenses (including attorney fees) or admonishment should not be imposed, with specified briefing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this Decision PQA and VLSI were ordered to each file a 15-page brief within 7 calendar days addressing whether PQA should be admonished or pay compensatory expenses; detailed billing statements and declaratory evidence may be filed as exhibits and excluded from page limit; 5-page responsive briefs allowed within 7 days of the initial briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence needed to support fee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: If fees are sought as compensatory expenses, parties should support requests with detailed billing statements and declaratory evidence as to the time and amount of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed billing statements and declarations may be filed as exhibits (excluded from page limits) and will be evaluated to determine appropriate time periods and amounts for fee assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning against withholding third-party communications absent waiver confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: A party offered to produce responsive third-party communications only if the Office confirmed such production would not be treated as waiver of objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's Scheduling Order warned that attempts to withhold evidence based on narrow interpretations may be sanctionable; parties should seek explicit waiver protections if concerned and log withheld documents with privilege logs rather than unilaterally withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factors for discretionary denial in presence of parallel district court litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering discretionary denial under the Apple Inc. v. Fintiv framework, relevant factors include the advanced stage of district court litigation, scheduled trial dates relative to PTAB deadlines, and overlap between issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's Guidance Memo instructs the PTAB to 'consider[] the merits of a petitioner’s challenge when determining whether to institute a post-grant proceeding in view of parallel district court litigation' and to allow 'compelling, meritorious challenges' to proceed despite parallel litigation. Board must balance patent-quality goals against potential abuse of repeated attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to § 315(b) one-year time bar for joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute (35 U.S.C. § 315(b)) expressly provides that the one-year time limitation shall not apply to a request for joinder under subsection (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may grant joinder even when a petition would otherwise be time-barred; joinder practice must still consider potential for abuse and the equities (e.g., references to General Plastic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of consistency across filings when evaluating truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency (or inconsistency) of a party's characterizations across the petition, declarations, interrogatory responses, and other filings is material when assessing whether statements are misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistent statements (e.g., claiming exclusivity in petition/declaration, later saying exclusivity was waivable, later saying they did not intend to waive) can indicate misleading argument or misrepresentation. The Office will examine the sequence and context of statements to determine sanctionability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential remedial measures proportional to misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies for sanctionable conduct should suit the wrongdoing and can range from admonishment/reprimand to compensatory expenses, dismissal as a party, holding facts established, or other appropriate sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will ensure remedy suits wrongdoing both in the specific case and as precedent for deterring similar misconduct; § 42.12(b) and case law (Voip-Pal.com, Inc.) support non-exhaustive sanctioning powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction review includes factual and legal submissions including non-declaratory evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When ordered to show cause, parties should support positions with briefing and non-declaratory evidence addressing whether conduct constituted abuse of process or otherwise thwarts the goals of the Office/AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scheduling Order invited parties to support arguments 'including through new arguments and non-declaratory evidence' and allowed amici briefing. Parties should use documentary evidence, interrogatory responses, and declarations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning that successful institution decision may not preclude later sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision to institute an IPR (based on merits at the time of institution) does not immunize a petitioner from later sanctions for misconduct (e.g., failure to comply with discovery or misrepresentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director declined to reverse Institution Decision despite dismissing PQA for misconduct, noting institution was supported by compelling merits 'at the time of Institution.' Thus, parties can be sanctioned post-institution if subsequent misconduct is established.
